sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Label look options
sections.what: Defines how each badge type looks: a primary color, a secondary color, a red destructive color, and an outline style. It also keeps the label on one line and adds a small hover effect.
sections.why: Keeps every tag on the site using one set of looks. The platform-tagged comments say what was changed from the standard version, but not why.
sections.watch_out: Labels never wrap, so long text can run past the edge of the box.

sections.name: BadgeProps
sections.title: Badge settings
sections.what: Lists the settings a badge accepts. These are the same as a plain box, plus the variant choice.
sections.why: Lets developers see what can be passed in.

sections.name: Badge
sections.title: The badge box
sections.what: Draws the small rounded label in the chosen look and passes any extra attributes through to the box.
sections.why: Keeps the badge a thin wrapper so pages can add their own attributes.
sections.watch_out: Styling a page adds is applied after the built-in look, so it can override the badge's rules.

summary: A small rounded label used to tag items, such as a status or a category, in four looks.
purpose: Shows a short piece of status or category text on screen, for example next to a name.
why: Comments tagged with a platform marker describe edits made to the standard version of this component. The reasons for those edits are not stated in the code.
how: Step 1: Defines the four looks: default, secondary, destructive and outline. Step 2: Lists the settings a badge accepts. Step 3: Draws the label box with the chosen look and passes other attributes through.
inputs: The label content, an optional variant, and any extra style classes or attributes.
outputs: A small rounded label on screen in the chosen color.
risks: Labels never wrap, so a long word runs past the edge of its box instead of breaking onto a new line.
debug: If the label looks wrong, check the variant passed in and whether the page adds conflicting classes. If the hover effect does nothing, check that the project's hover-elevate style exists.
